classification.difficultyReason: Derive missing angles using triangle angle sums and isosceles properties before testing congruence.

content.prompt:
Decide if each pair of triangles is congruent.
You first need to use the angle sum of a triangle to help calculate some of the angles.

spec.description: Side-by-side sideways isosceles triangles pointing towards one another, with double ticks on all four sloping sides.
spec.mathematics: The left apex angle is 100 degrees. The right upper base angle is 40 degrees. All four double-ticked sides are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied angles and equal-side markings are visible.

answer.worked:
The right triangle is isosceles, so both base angles are $40^\circ$.
$$180^\circ-40^\circ-40^\circ=100^\circ.$$
Both triangles have two corresponding equal sides and the included angle $100^\circ$. They are congruent by SAS.

spec.description: An upward-pointing and a downward-pointing isosceles triangle, paired horizontally.
spec.mathematics: All four sloping sides carry double ticks. The left lower-left base angle is 75 degrees; the right bottom apex angle is 35 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Derived angles and congruence decision are hidden.

answer.worked:
The left triangle has equal base angles of $75^\circ$, so its apex angle is
$$180^\circ-75^\circ-75^\circ=30^\circ.$$
The included angles between the marked equal sides are $30^\circ$ and $35^\circ$. The triangles are not congruent.

spec.description: Left triangle with horizontal bottom side and right triangle with horizontal top side; labels remain attached to their source vertices and sides.
spec.mathematics: Left: 50-degree upper-left angle, 100-degree lower-left angle and 5 cm bottom side. Right: 30-degree upper-left angle, 100-degree upper-right angle and 5 cm top side.

answer.worked:
The remaining angle in the left triangle is
$$180^\circ-50^\circ-100^\circ=30^\circ.$$
The remaining angle in the right triangle is
$$180^\circ-30^\circ-100^\circ=50^\circ.$$
The triangles have matching angles and a corresponding side of $5\text{ cm}$ between the $30^\circ$ and $100^\circ$ angles. They are congruent by AAS.

spec.description: Two differently oriented right triangles with their original right-angle squares, angle labels and 10 cm side labels.
spec.mathematics: Left: 35-degree upper angle, lower-right right angle and 10 cm side joining these vertices. Right: upper right angle, lower-left angle 65 degrees and upper-to-lower-right side 10 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Missing angles and decision are not supplied.

answer.worked:
The remaining angle in the left triangle is
$$180^\circ-90^\circ-35^\circ=55^\circ.$$
The remaining angle in the right triangle is
$$180^\circ-90^\circ-65^\circ=25^\circ.$$
Their angle sets are $35^\circ,55^\circ,90^\circ$ and $25^\circ,65^\circ,90^\circ$. The triangles are not congruent.
